theories.hypothesis: Humor arises when an established mental model is violated by facts that refuse to fit it.
A reveal that forces the audience to reinterpret everything that came before outperforms bare surprise.
A violation is funny only when simultaneously perceived as safe, distant, or alternatively interpretable; distance moves the sweet spot.
Creativity and humor arise when two previously separate conceptual frames collide on a shared structure.
A character whose defining trait conflicts with their role, species or job outperforms generic absurdity.
The powerful diminished beats the weak mocked; inversion of who controls whom is inherently comic.
A character who understands the absurdity of its own identity and exploits it beats one who is merely absurd.
A person or institution mechanically following a rule after reality makes it absurd is inherently comic (Bergson).
Letting the audience share privileged knowledge against someone in the scene multiplies any other mechanism.
Establish a rule, repeat it, mutate it, escalate it; the third beat must break the pattern.
What a character claims to be diverging from what everyone can see it is creates sustained comic tension.
Replacing a generic category with an unusually concrete person, object, place or detail upgrades any joke (GTVH script opposition needs specific scripts).
Treating metaphor, rhetoric or policy language as physically true generates comic collisions for free.
Placing two states side by side (before/after, expectation/reality) lets the gap do the joking.
Following a pattern to step 2, 3 and 10 finds premises hiding past the obvious stop.
